name: AX30G Hyper Resonator (HYPR), measured 2026-09-18
notes: Derivation, every candidate with its residual, and what is under-determined: docs/hypr-model-2026-09-18.md. C++ port spec: docs/hypr-cpp-spec.md. Measured from the 21 captures of capture/grids/hypr.json (2026-09-18, 20 IN-LIN + 1 IN-MAX_take2, Block 1 only).

Block diagram: out = Direct*x + Effect*RES(DRIVER(x), f(E)). DRIVER = gain g(Type,Harmonics) -> mix of a symmetric hard clip (odd) and a DC-blocked full-wave rectifier (even). RES = 2-pole resonant low-pass at f(E), Q(Resonance), cascaded with a fixed 2-pole low-pass at 5706 Hz.

The resonator's rest frequency is 389 Hz. Measured three ways that agree to 0.2 %: the Resonance-25/Resonance-0 noise-TF ratio peaks at 388.5 Hz, the Resonance-50/Resonance-0 ratio at 388.1 Hz, and a free filter fit to the near-linear Type-1/Harmonics-0 response puts the resonant pole at 388-396 Hz.

Resonance changes ONLY the height of that narrow peak and nothing else: the R25/R0 and R50/R0 noise-TF ratios are flat to +-0.5 dB everywhere from 40 Hz to 6 kHz except within about a third of an octave of 389 Hz, where they read +5.6 dB and +23.5 dB. maps.q converts those peak heights into Q via peak ~= Q; Q(50) = 64 is a LOWER BOUND because the +23.5 dB was read on 1/17-octave bands and the true peak is narrower than one band.

The block runs in the PRE-EMPHASISED domain and its output is NOT de-emphasised. Measured on the Direct-only capture (Direct 50 / Effect 0) against the LIN Bypass capture: +0.5 dB at 1.1 kHz, +1.4 at 1.7 k, +3.0 at 2.8 k, +5.1 at 4.4 k, +7.1 at 7.0 k, +8.5 at 11.1 k, +9.2 at 17.6 k, on the noise, sweep and DI segments independently and identically, against the input stage's own pre-emphasis shelf at +0.1/+1.0/+2.5/+4.6/+6.7/+8.4/+9.5. So input_stage.de_emphasis = 'after_effect' (render.py defers the filter) and blocks.output_de_emphasis = 'none' (engine/hypr.py re-applies the pre-emphasis at its output so the deferred filter cancels exactly). No other measured block behaves this way -- the 3BEQ's flat row divided by Bypass is flat to 0.35 dB.

Direct Level is linear in the displayed value: Direct 25 against Direct 50 measures -5.9 dB on the ramp where 20*log10(25/50) = -6.02. Effect Level is ASSUMED to follow the same law -- the grid has no pair that isolates it.

The Direct path is otherwise a clean copy: its ramp tracks the Bypass capture's within 0.4 dB over the whole -40..0 dBFS range, and its noise/sweep/DI transfer functions are flat to 0.3 dB below 700 Hz.

The driver table is FITTED, not derived. g, w_odd and w_even per (Type, Harmonics) were fitted by rendering a 1 kHz -20 dBFS sine through the input stage, the driver and the resonator and matching the measured steady-state H1..H7 of the six R0 captures: 6.25 dB rms over 42 harmonic levels spanning 60 dB, with one shared output gain (blocks.resonator.gain_db). It reproduces the three qualitative facts the captures establish -- Type 1 / Harmonics 0 is nearly linear and 50 dB down (H1 -77.4 dBFS, every harmonic below -104), Type 1 / Harmonics 50 is almost purely EVEN (H2 -67.8 with H1 -87.2 and H3 -88.3, i.e. a frequency doubler), and Type 2 is clip-dominated at every Harmonics (Type 2 / Harmonics 0 is pure odd: H1 -47.0, H3 -76.8, H5 -90.3, H7 -98.3) -- but it misses Type 1 / Harmonics 50's fundamental by 21 dB and Type 1 / Harmonics 25's by 11 dB.

The driver ends in a HARD CLIP. The Type-2 / Harmonics-0 ramp is the cleanest evidence in the campaign: the 1 kHz output rises exactly 1:1 from -69.4 dBFS at -39 dBFS in to -54.2 at -23.6, then is FLAT at -53.5 +- 0.1 dB for the remaining 22 dB of input. The third harmonic is flat at -82.9 over the same span, i.e. H3/H1 = -29.4 dB where an analytic hard clip driven far past threshold gives -9.5 dB and a 2-pole low-pass at 389 Hz takes off another 19 dB at 3 kHz. H5/H1 and H7/H1 follow the same accounting to 1.4 and 0.6 dB. That is what fixes the resonator's slope at 12 dB/oct through 1-7 kHz.

The sweep: the corner does not move at all below about -34 dBFS of input peak envelope, then rises steeply. Measured on the DI clip of the all-up row (Type 2, Harmonics 50, Sensitivity 50, Depth 50, Resonance 50) by binning the output spectrogram's peak frequency against the input's peak envelope: 375 Hz flat from -60 to -33 dBFS, 750 Hz at -33..-30, 3656 Hz at -30..-27, 4641 Hz at -27..-24. Row 21 (Sensitivity 25, otherwise similar) gives 516 / 1547 / 3984 Hz in the same bins. blocks.sweep.octaves_per_db 0.80 is the Sensitivity-50 slope; maps.sens carries 25 -> 0.69 from row 21 and 10 -> 0.35 as a GUESS.

maps.depth is a straight line and is NOT measured: Depth 25 and Depth 50 put the ramp's 1 kHz crossing at -19.4 and -19.1 dBFS, 0.3 dB apart, which does not constrain a law. Worse, Sensitivity 10 / 25 / 50 put it at -19.1 / -19.1 / -18.9 dBFS -- no Sensitivity dependence at all on those rows, which contradicts the DI measurement above. The reason is almost certainly that all seven sweep rows sit at Type 1 / Harmonics 0, where the driver output is 50 dB down and there is nothing for the resonator to resonate on; capture/grids/hypr-2.json moves the sweep axis onto Type 2 / Harmonics 50.

maps.release_tau_ms (the Decay control) is three points chosen to reproduce a coarse observation and is the weakest law in the model: on the ramp, Decay 0 and Decay 25 put the 1 kHz crossing 98 ms apart (2.513 s and 2.611 s after the ramp starts) and Decay 50 has no crossing at all -- its output is already elevated 8 dB at the bottom of the ramp, 1.5 s after the previous segment ended, which is what a release of order a second looks like. Attack was not measured at all (the burst onsets are at the noise floor on every sweep row) and is carried at the compressor's measured 1.2 ms.

Polarity DOWN inverts the sign of the octave excursion about the same 389 Hz rest. Evidence: the DOWN capture's DI-segment spectrogram peak sits at 188-234 Hz where the UP capture's sits at 375 Hz and above, and its ramp output rises smoothly with no 1 kHz crossing (the corner is moving away from 1 kHz, not through it). Whether DOWN has the same range as UP is NOT established.

The IN-MAX row: use AX30G_HYPR_..._IN-MAX_take2.wav. The take-1 MAX file is byte-for-byte equivalent in level to the LIN row (its segment levels match the LIN capture to 0.1 dB on every segment) -- it was captured before the input knob was moved, and must be ignored.

NOT modelled, and the largest single discrepancy: a steady 1 kHz tone and a 1 kHz tone ramping through the same level give different harmonic structure by up to 25 dB, on rows where Depth is 0 and the corner should not be moving. Type 1 / Harmonics 50 reads H1 -87.2 / H2 -67.8 on the steady -20 dBFS sine and H1 -63.1 / H2 -87.6 as the ramp passes -20.5 dBFS -- the two harmonics swap places. The output settles to its steady value about 0.6 s after a tone starts, so there is a slow state in the block that this model does not have.

blocks.resonator.gain_db is the effect path's own output scaling and is ARBITRARY: the fit that produced the driver table wanted -18.96 dB, which puts the all-up row's peak 4.4 dB over full scale in the renderer, so it ships 12 dB lower (-30.96) to keep the 18-bit converter out of the way. Relative levels between rows are unchanged, and tests/hypr_null.py fits one broadband gain per row anyway.
